extracted.intended_audience: users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (algebraic geometers / computational algebraists) who run/interpret resolution routines and reszeta.lib procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation excerpt showing the textual output format used by SINGULAR resolution routines (chart-by-chart logs) and short library procedure docs (e.g., computeN). Useful for understanding each reported field when running resolve/related libraries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overview of Current Chart
rubrics_metrics.description: A short summary header printed for each chart showing: Current number of final charts; Total number of charts currently in chart-tree; Index of the current chart in chart-tree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example lines printed repeatedly: 'Current number of final charts: N', 'Total number of charts currently in chart-tree: M', 'Index of the current chart in chart-tree: K'. Use these three fields to track progress of the resolution across charts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambient Space
rubrics_metrics.description: The ambient space for the current chart, printed as one or more equalities (e.g. '_[1]=0').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows the defining ambient equation(s) for the chart (often '_[1]=0' in examples). Appears at the start of each chart's output under the heading 'Ambient Space:'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideal of Variety
rubrics_metrics.description: The (single) ideal element describing the variety in the current chart, printed as '_[1]=<polynomial expression>'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show explicit polynomial(s) (sometimes long multi-line polynomials). This field gives the transformed defining equation(s) of the variety in the current chart and is used to inspect progress of the resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptional Divisors
rubrics_metrics.description: List of exceptional divisors present in the current chart, printed as numbered entries like '[1]:', '[2]:', etc., or 'empty list'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be an empty list or contain several entries; the printed block indicates which exceptional divisors (if any) appear in this chart. Useful to identify existing blowup divisors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Images of variables of original ring
rubrics_metrics.description: The images (transformations) of the original ring variables in the current chart, printed as indexed entries e.g. '_[1]=...', '_[2]=...', '_[3]=...'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each entry shows how an original variable maps into the local coordinates of the chart (often polynomials in the chart variables x(i), y(j)). Use this to follow coordinate changes and substitutions applied by blowups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upcoming Center
rubrics_metrics.description: The center(s) chosen for the next blowup(s), printed under 'Upcoming Center' as one or more indexed polynomial equalities (e.g. '_[1]=<expr>', '_[2]=<expr>').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This block indicates which polynomial(s) or locus will be used as center for the next resolution step (next blowup). It is printed before the separator line and helps to anticipate the next chart transformations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure computeN(L,DL)
rubrics_metrics.description: Library procedure from reszeta.lib. Signature shown as 'computeN(L,DL);' with parameters: L = list of rings; DL = divisor list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return type described: 'intvec, i-th entry is multiplicity of i-th divisor in total transform under resolution'. Usage context: L has structure of output of resolve, DL has structure of output of prepEmbDiv. Example invocation pattern shown in the appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing divisor list and computing vector (prepEmbDiv / computeV example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Example usage snippet: 'iden=prepEmbDiv(re); intvec v=computeV(re, iden); v;' showing preparation of embedded-divisor data and then computing a vector v (example output: '3,5,8,11,1').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The snippet demonstrates the workflow: call prepEmbDiv on a resolve output to get an identifier/list of divisors, then call computeV (or similar) to obtain an integer vector summarizing divisor-related quantities. The example return '3,5,8,11,1' shows the form of the intvec but the page gives no further formal description of computeV's semantics beyond the example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolve run completion indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Console messages indicating resolution status such as '============= result will be tested ==========' and 'the number of charts obtained: N' and final 'result is o.k.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These textual lines denote internal checks and finality of a resolve run; 'the number of charts obtained' reports the total final charts counted, and 'result is o.k.' signals successful completion of the procedure's internal tests.
